title: Brazil2026ElectionFilter is registered unconditionally with no feature-switch gate
claim: Brazil2026ElectionFilter exists, is registered in the pre-scoring filter list of PhoenixCandidatePipeline, and does not override the Filter trait's enable() method, so it inherits the trait default of unconditional true -- unlike other request-path features (e.g. BidirectionalFollowHydrator) that are explicitly gated by a named param.
runtime_caveats: No checked-in evidence bounds who is in BRAZIL_2026_ELECTION_USER_IDS beyond the hardcoded static set; the list's currency/accuracy relative to the actual Electoral Court reporting is not verifiable from source.
Whether this code path is actually invoked for real Brazilian users in production, and under what request-routing/geo conditions, is not established by the checked-in filter alone.
notes: Legal/political special case per lens L06. S00 records only that the code exists, is registered, and has no local runtime gate; it does not and cannot establish production activation, and does not assert any legal conclusion.

title: README's Pre-Scoring Filters table omits Brazil2026ElectionFilter
claim: The root README's 'Pre-Scoring Filters' table (17 rows) does not list Brazil2026ElectionFilter, even though the same README's 'Latest Updates' section describes that filter in detail and the filter is actually present in the pipeline's pre-scoring filter Vec, positioned between AuthorSocialgraphFilter and VideoFilter.

source_evidence.symbol_or_section: How It Works - Filtering - Pre-Scoring Filters table

notes: Internal documentation inconsistency within the same README: the filter is called out prominently elsewhere in the same document but omitted from the definitive ordered filter table. Also observed: home-mixer/filters/mod.rs declares several additional filter modules (ad_adjacent_served_filter, following_retweet_deduplication_filter, invalid_conversation_module_filter, push_to_home_dedup_filter, result_size_filter, self_reply_chain_filter) not present in the README's pre-scoring table; S00 did not determine which pipeline stage each belongs to, so this is not claimed as a further contradiction, only flagged for S02.

title: README's illustrative '468x' weight example exactly matches current checked-in ReportWeight/FavoriteWeight ratio
claim: The README's misconception explanation uses the specific number '468' as an example of a report-to-like weight ratio; the current checked-in constants are ReportWeight = -234.0 and FavoriteWeight = 0.5, whose magnitude ratio is exactly 468 (234 / 0.5 = 468).
runtime_caveats: This is the checked-in default only; the actual runtime value used for any given production request could differ via feature-switch override.
notes: Worth flagging because it shows the doc's example number is not an arbitrary round figure chosen purely for pedagogy -- it is traceable to a specific, currently-checked-in pair of constants. This strengthens (but does not by itself prove) the doc's implicit claim that the example reflects real production-relevant weight values.

title: Checked-in BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost default reflects the doc's July 24 value (15.0), not its July 13 value (20.0)
claim: docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md shows two sequential diffs to BidirectionalFollowReplyWeightBoost's default: 20.0 (introduced July 13) then changed to 15.0 (July 24). The current snapshot's param.rs contains only the end state, 15.0.
runtime_caveats: This confirms the checked-in DEFAULT only. It does not by itself prove that 15.0 is the value actually served to any given production user, since xai_feature_switches allows runtime override of param defaults.
notes: This is the clearest example in S00's scope of the README's claim (checked-in defaults are periodically synced to reflect production values) being consistent with an observable, checked-in artifact, for one specific parameter. It does not verify the cron-sync mechanism itself (see S00-F013), only that the end value in the snapshot matches the doc's narrated end state.

title: BidirectionalFollowDwellWeightBoost checked-in default remains 0.0 (no-op), consistent with 'not shipped more broadly' claim
claim: BidirectionalFollowDwellWeightBoost's checked-in default is 0.0, and dwell_weight_for() only applies the boost when the value is nonzero, so the dwell-boost code path is present but inert at the current checked-in default.
runtime_caveats: A zero checked-in default does not preclude a nonzero runtime override being active for some experiment population; the snapshot cannot see feature-switch state.
notes: Reachability chain (L03): DECLARED, EXPORTED, CONSTRUCTED, CALLED all proven; ENABLE CONDITION (nonzero boost) is checked-in FALSE by default, so the code is currently a documented no-op absent runtime override.

title: Current bidirectional_follow_hydrator.rs has materially diverged from the diff shown in docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md
claim: The doc's July 13 diff shows BidirectionalFollowHydrator gating solely on EnableBidirectionalFollowHydration and checking mutual-follow status only for authors the viewer already follows. The current checked-in file additionally: (a) imports and reads a second param, EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration (checked-in default true), which -- when true -- expands the author-check set to ALL candidate authors rather than only followed ones; (b) adds a `!query.has_cached_posts` condition to enable(), so the hydrator is skipped when the query already has cached posts; (c) introduces and populates a new candidate field, author_follows_viewer, that is not mentioned in the doc or the README.
runtime_caveats: The doc explicitly frames itself as a historical, illustrative example ('here's what you might've seen'), dated to a July 2026 diff, while the snapshot is captured 2026-08-14/15; some evolution beyond the shown diff is therefore expected and not itself a defect.
The extent to which EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration's true default is itself a later runtime-configured value vs. a fixed checked-in decision is not established beyond the param.rs text.
notes: See also S00-F007. A reader relying on the docs/BIDIRECTIONAL_BOOST_CHANGE.md diff as a literal, current description of the hydrator's behavior would be materially misled about what the file currently does. This is documentation drift (lens L18), not a code defect.

title: New author_follows_viewer signal feeds the Phoenix ranking model as an input feature, undocumented in README or the bidirectional-boost doc
claim: The candidate field author_follows_viewer (populated by BidirectionalFollowHydrator when EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration is true) is read in home-mixer/models/candidate.rs's feature-conversion method and mapped into xai_recsys_proto::AuthorInfo.is_following_user, which is part of the feature payload constructed for Phoenix. This is a second, distinct consumption path for the mutual/one-directional-follow signal beyond the documented ranking_scorer.rs reply/dwell weight boost.

source_evidence.symbol_or_section: How It Works - Scoring and Ranking

runtime_caveats: S00 did not trace how (or whether) Phoenix's model actually uses AuthorInfo.is_following_user internally; that is Phoenix model/feature-provenance territory (S05/S06), not established here.

EnableAllAuthorFollowHydration's checked-in default is true, but S00 did not verify whether this path is exercised in the same request flow as the documented reply/dwell boost or is a separate/newer initiative.
notes: This is an example of 'source reveals an undocumented behavioral component' (S00 findings criteria, section 19). It should be a priority item for S05's Phoenix feature-provenance review, since a follow-relationship feature feeding the model directly is a materially different mechanism from a fixed post-hoc weight boost and was not flagged anywhere in the two S00-assigned documents that discuss this exact feature area.

title: BidirectionalFollowHydrator's failure behavior on social-graph client error is not fully traceable within S00 scope
claim: When socialgraph_client.check_followed_by errors, BidirectionalFollowHydrator::hydrate returns Err(e.to_string()) for every candidate in the batch. What the candidate-pipeline framework does with a per-candidate hydration Err (drop the candidate, use a default value, fail the whole pipeline stage, retry) is defined by the Hydrator trait/execution engine in candidate-pipeline/, not in this file.
runtime_caveats: Fail-open vs fail-closed behavior for this hydrator's errors is unresolved by S00 and requires reading candidate-pipeline/hydrator.rs's execution engine, which is out of S00's assigned scope.
notes: Lens L04 (failure/fallback behavior) obligation recorded for S01.

title: GrowthBook is a real, wired external runtime-configuration dependency, but only directly evidenced in abuse-enforcement-service, not home-mixer
claim: abuse-enforcement-service/service-lib/src/growthbook.rs and growthbook_writer.rs implement a full GrowthBookClient integration (read config, write config, admin API with a protected endpoint) used by that service. home-mixer/params/param.rs instead binds its param!() defaults to the xai_feature_switches crate, a different runtime-override mechanism. The README's general 'configuration system' language (Experiments and Configuration section) does not name either mechanism explicitly.
runtime_caveats: S00 did not exhaustively search every component for its own runtime-config mechanism; only home-mixer and abuse-enforcement-service were checked directly. Other components (e.g. Phoenix serving, visibility-filtering) may use yet other mechanisms not catalogued here.
missing_dependencies: The external GrowthBook service itself (its URL, keys, and the actual config values it serves) is not part of this repository and cannot be reconstructed from source.
notes: Directly substantiates the architecture map's D17/'GrowthBook' cross-cutting note and is important evidence for the 'Public Snapshot vs Production Reality' section: at least one safety-critical component's runtime behavior is provably controlled by an external, unpublished config service that this repository can write to as well as read from.

title: Grox prompt-omission claim is self-documented in the checked-in source
claim: grox/flows/upa/prompts.py loads Jinja2 templates from a 'templates' subdirectory that does not exist anywhere in the snapshot (no .j2 file exists under grox/ at all), and the file contains an inline comment explicitly stating: 'As stated in README for the open source repo, prompts are excluded to reduce gameability of the system.'
missing_dependencies: grox/flows/upa/templates/ (and equivalent template directories for reply_spam and ptos flows) are absent from the snapshot.
notes: Rare case of a checked-in code comment directly and explicitly corroborating a root README transparency claim from inside the affected component itself.

title: phoenix/NOTICE documents third-party BSD-3-Clause and Apache-2.0 code bundled inside phoenix/xrex, qualifying a blanket 'whole repo is Apache-2.0' reading
claim: phoenix/NOTICE lists numerous files under phoenix/xrex/cutedsl/ranker_fa4/ and phoenix/xrex/pallas/ as derived from flash-attention and NVIDIA CUTLASS (BSD-3-Clause) and jax-triton (Apache-2.0), each retaining its own original license notice in-file per the NOTICE file's own description.
notes: The root LICENSE (Apache-2.0) is not contradicted -- Apache-2.0 explicitly permits bundling differently-licensed dependencies alongside a NOTICE file -- but a claim reduction of 'this whole repository is Apache-2.0, full stop' would be an incomplete reading. Only phoenix/ was found to carry a NOTICE file; no other component-level LICENSE/NOTICE files exist in the snapshot.

title: phoenix-rankall-strato's visibility-filtering consultation is gated behind a decider flag, not proven unconditional
claim: phoenix-rankall-strato/lib/eventProcessing.strato consults a visibility/shouldDropTweet path, but the call is wrapped in a check of decider flag enable_vf_rust_should_drop_tweet, whose value is not established by this snapshot.
runtime_caveats: Decider flag default/runtime value is external to this snapshot (deciders are a separate config mechanism from the xai_feature_switches params seen in home-mixer).
missing_dependencies: The decider configuration system's actual values are not part of the repository.
notes: Confirms the cross-domain bridge documented in _analysis/architecture/CROSS_DOMAIN_SYSTEMS.md exists at the code level; does not confirm it is always active.

title: The README's claimed cron-based mechanism for syncing production param values into checked-in defaults has no corresponding artifact anywhere in the snapshot
claim: README.md states: 'we run cron scripts that set the defaults in this repository's code to be the primary production values.' A repository-wide search for 'cron' (case-sensitive, across all tracked source, config, and doc files) returns only this sentence in README.md itself; no script, workflow file, CI job, or scheduled-task definition implementing such a sync exists in the frozen snapshot.
runtime_caveats: Absence of an in-repo cron script is expected if the sync job itself runs in unpublished internal infrastructure (consistent with the README's own 'What's not in this repo?' framing about deployment-related code); this finding does not claim the mechanism doesn't exist, only that it is not independently verifiable from the published snapshot.
missing_dependencies: The cron/sync job implementation itself is not published.
notes: This is the central evidentiary gap underlying the entire repository's claim that 'checked-in defaults reflect production values.' Every other finding in S00 that treats a checked-in default as production-representative (e.g. S00-F004) inherits this same caveat and should not be read as independently proving production state.
